chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.content:
Jackpot of Vengeance Iris Nyte Chapter 1 Mom's anxious face filled my vision, her voice sharpening from distant static into something painfully real. "Zara, what did you need to tell me? If you have something to say, hurry up. Your dad's waiting for me to get home and cook. You said earlier that you won something. What did you win?" Hearing her questions, I quickly scanned my surroundings. My apartment. Understanding hit instantly. Thad been reborn. In my previous life, at this exact moment, I had just won a $30 -million jackpot.

All I could think about was taking my mom, Helena Nightfall, away from that miserable household, moving somewhere far away, and starting a new life with her. She had agreed again and again. But the moment my dad, Victor Nightfall, came home, she told him everything. My gambling addict dad's eyes had lit up like a predator spotting prey. He marched straight up to me and demanded the ticket. "Where is it? Hand it over! So you hit the jackpot and didn't tell your old man? Planning to run off with your mom? "You ungrateful little brat. Your money is my money.

How dare you make decisions on your own?" Step by step, he closed in, forcing me to give it up. As if would ever let him have it. I had won that money. With it, [could finally escape that house. I would never again have to hand over my salary and scrape by on whatever scraps he allowed me to keep. No matter what he said, I refused. So he started hitting me. While he beat me, Mom had slipped into my room, rummaged through my things, found my debit card, and walked out with it. Dad took the money and went straight back to gambling.

Only then did Mom come to my side, speaking in a hushed voice, " Zara, don't blame me. I'm doing this for your own good. You're a girl. What would you even do with that kind of money? It's safer in your dad's hands. "In this family, your dad should be the one in charge." After saying that, she left without another glance, abandoning me where I lay bruised and swollen. Later, Dad used the money to indulge himself at luxury clubs. He bragged nonstop in the family group chat, and relatives from back home flooded in to flatter him.

His vanity satisfied, he started lending money out left and right. Unwilling to watch my winnings be squandered, I went to confront him and demand it back. By sheer coincidence, I ran into his creditors. An argument broke out. In the chaos, he shoved me out the door along with them. The debt collectors had lost all reason. Ignoring my pleas, they stabbed me to death on the spot. All of this began because Mom told him. So this time, I would guard that money with my life and live freely on my own terms. u (aig Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.content:
Chapter 2 Hearing the faint complaint in Mom's voice, I blinked and tossed out a casual lie. "Mom, I meant Iwon an air fryer at the office party. Iwas asking if you wanted it." She rolled her eyes. "Oh, an air fryer? The way you sounded, I thought you'd won the lottery." My chest tightened. "As if. If] had that kind of luck, I'd be thrilled." "Still, since you won something, maybe I'll ride your good fortune and buy a ticket later. Who knows, maybe I'll win too. If we really did win, your dad would have money and wouldn't hit me anymore. "Alright, alright. Where's the fryer? Bring it out.

I'll take it home and make him fried chicken." Talmost laughed at the irony. Even after being beaten, she still rushed back to him like a lovesick fool. In my past life, 1 must have been out of my mind to tell her about the jackpot. Back then, when I told her, she had grabbed my hands and smiled so brightly. What I hadn't realized was that she wasn't happy for me-she was happy for him. Dad would always come first in her heart. Despite being her daughter, I was nothing more than a cash machine. She probably decided to tell him the moment she learned I'd won.

She just couldn't show it in front of me. As soonas Dad got home, she had told him everything. I was packing when someone knocked on my door. I thought it was Mom coming back. Instead, Dad had come to rob me. The memory made me take a deep breath. I quickly handed her the air fryer. Pd bought it a couple of days earlier, planning to bring it home eventually. I never expected it to come in handy like this. The moment she left, I started packing to get out of here. Thad already claimed the $30 million. After taxes, $24 million remained. All of it was still in my account.

Remembering what happened in my previous life, I decided to open several new bank accounts and split the money up, just in case. That afternoon, I finished setting everything up. I was just thinking about where to travel in a few days when I suddenly got a call from my cousin, Kellan Nightfall. "Zara, did you win the lottery? $30 million?" My grip on the phone nearly slipped. This time, I hadn't told anyone. How did he know? Wait. He was back in our hometown, Graves Hollow, and not even here in Blackridge City. How could he possibly know? Had he seen me at the claims center?

My palms grew slick with sweat, but I forced myself to sound calm. "How could that be? You know me. My luck's always terrible. No way I'd win anything, let alone $30 million. Stop messing with me." I laughed it off and tried to hang up, but his tone turned firm. " Zara, it was definitely you. I saw it." He saw me? Inearly cried out, quickly digging my nails into my palm to steady myself. "I've been home these past couple of days. I haven't gone anywhere. Maybe you mistook someone else for me?" Kellan chuckled. "If it wasn't you, why are you so nervous? Look at the photo I just sent.

Isn't that you?" My phone buzzed as the message came through. Iopened it, and instantly, all the warmth drained from my body.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.content:
Chapter 3 Indeed, I was the person in the photo. Still, Ihad been wrapped up so tightly, dressed in baggy clothes with everything concealed, that my figure was impossible to make out. Nonetheless, anyone close to me would recognize me instantly. My heart pounded as I scrambled for an excuse. Kellan spoke again on the other end, "Zara, you've got all that money now. Transfer a million or two to this good cousin of yours. Share your fortune." Ibarely stopped myself from swearing. Shameless. The nerve of him. Amillion or two? Why didn't he just rob a bank? I forced myself to calm down.

"That isn't me. You're mistaken. I have something to do. 'm hanging up." Iwas about to end the call when his voice turned threatening. "Zara, if you don't send it, 'll tell everyone. Let's see if you can still keep that money safe then. And don't forget, your dad is drowning in debt." He hung up immediately. I paced the room, furious, until I finally forced myself to calm down. No. Thad to leave now. If Kellan could recognize me, others could too. And once that happened, there would be no way I could keep the money. Thurriedly packed, planning to move out the next day.

What I didn't expect was how fast he would act. That very night, Dad showed up. He hada key to my apartment, and he let himself in without knocking. Iwas watching TV when I heard the door open. jumped in shock, and the moment I saw him, a bad feeling settled in my chest. Sure enough, he started shouting immediately, "Zara! Hand over the money! "You win the lottery and dare to hide it from your own father? You've got some nerve! If Kellan hadn't called me, I wouldn't even know about it." Achill ran down my spine. That fool. When I refused to give him money, he went straight to Dad.

What was I supposed to do now? Was I going to lose everything again? My heart raced as I tried to think of a solution, but Dad didn't give me the chance. He grabbed the broom by the door and swung it at me. Caught off guard, I took the blow head-on. Then he stepped forward and kicked me hard in the chest. His fists came down next-heavy, relentless. The difference in strength was overwhelming. I couldn't escape, so I could only curl up and endure it. At that moment, Mom walked in. She spoke with a tone of reproach, "So this is why you wanted me earlier. You really did win the lottery.

"This girl, honestly. You win money and don't hand it over? Trying to keep it for yourself? You've got way too many ideas. You don't even consider the family at all. "Where is the money? I'll go get it. We can use it to pay off your dad's debts."" bit down hard on my teeth. Pd been given a second chance. There was no way I was letting them take it again. Right now, the priority was getting them out of here. I gasped through the pain and looked at Dad. "Dad, I didn't win anything! I don't even know how to buy lottery tickets. How could I have bought one? Maybe Kellan's lost his mind.

If I'd won, I would've handed the money over already." Dad clearly didn't believe me. "Bullshit! Kellan sent me the photo. One look and anyone can tell it's you. Still trying to lie? Hand it over now, or I'll beat you to death!" He raised his foot to kick me again. I shouted quickly, "Dad, I'm not lying. If you don't believe me, I'll get my debit card. You can check it yourself." He paused. I struggled to my feet and limped back to the bedroom. Slowly, deliberately, I took out my wallet. Dad strode over and snatched it from my hands. After rummaging through it, he found my debit card.

"What's the PIN?" Iclenched my jaw and gave him the six digits. He immediately took the card and walked out. Mom followed right behind him. u (aig Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.content:
Chapter 4 After they left, I shut the door and carefully made my way to the sofa, lowering myself down. Good thing I had acted quickly. I'd gone to the bank that afternoon and opened new accounts. Those cards were already hidden away. The only one in my wallet was my regular payroll card, and there wasn't much money in it. Even if they withdrew everything, they'd only find a few thousand dollars. That should be enough to throw them off. Sure enough, half an hour later, Dad came back, cursing under his breath. He had the card and some cash in his hand. "That brat Kellan only knows how to lie.

Got my hopes up for nothing. I withdrew everything. Here's your card." He tossed it onto the floor. I silently walked over and picked it up. Just as Dad was about to leave, Mom glanced toward my room. She spotted the suitcase and stopped him. "Victor, wait. She's packed. What if she transferred the money and is planning to run off?" My heart dropped. Dad turned around and saw the suitcase too. Rage flooded his face. "You little liar, you dare trick me? Where's the money? Hand it over right now, or I'll chop you up!" He kicked the suitcase over, then yanked it open.

Clothes spilled across the floor. Mom clapped her hands sharply when she saw them. "See? I told you she was lying! We saw the photo, and she still won't admit it. She's planning to go enjoy herself while abandoning us! "Zara, hand over the money. How much could a young woman like you possibly spend? We'll leave youa few tens of thousands. That's more than enough for the rest of your life." As she spoke, my gaze grew colder and colder. How had I never seen her true colors before? Dad moved toward me again, ready to hit me. I quickly pulled out my phone. "Dad, I have to go ona business trip.

The company just assigned it to me. I leave tomorrow morning. Look at the messages in the group chat." He snatched the phone, scrolling through it with a dark expression before tossing it back. His eyes bored into mine. "Tell me the truth, Zara. Did you win or not?" Ishook my head frantically. "No. Dad, why would I lie? My salary is barely anything each month. If I'd really won, I would've claimed it already. Why would I still be going ona business trip?" He stared at me without speaking. Mom muttered from the side, "Who knows if you have other cards?

Maybe you moved the money and are tricking us." My heart skipped a beat. "I'm not lying. If you don't believe me, search the place." Topened the bedroom door, acting completely indifferent. Dad exchanged a look with Mom. She rushed in and began tearing through my room. Fifteen minutes later, she came out, disappointment written all over her face. Seeing that, Dad threw out one last threat. "If you're lying, I'll chop you to pieces."" Then they left. The moment the door closed, my legs gave out, and I collapsed onto the floor. That was too close. I almost got exposed.

Icursed Kellan viciously in my head as I forced myself up and started repacking. I hadn't lied. The company really had assigned me to a business trip. When I saw the message earlier, I'd planned to refuse, but before I could reply, Dad and Mom had returned. Thank God I hadn't answered. Otherwise, everything would have been exposed. Looked like I couldn't quit my job after all. If l resigned now, that would truly be the end. As I considered my next move, my eyes landed on the clothes scattered from the suitcase. suddenly, inspiration struck. u (aig Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.content:
Chapter 5 The next day, I left on my business trip as scheduled. During the trip, Kellan called again with more threats. He was convinced I was the person in the photo, and he kept demanding money. Imade up a random excuse and hung up. After several attempts, he grew furious and threatened to post everything in the family group chat so everyone back in Graves Hollow could take their share. I told him to do whatever he wanted and ended the call. Since he couldn't get any money from me, he actually did it. He posted the photo in the family chat. The group exploded. Of course it did.

$30 million-who wouldn't be tempted? Calls poured in from every relative imaginable. Mom and Dad called too. I didn't answer a single one. I simply turned off my phone. I didn't need to guess. They were probably livid. But what did that have to do with me? I won that money fair and square. Why should I share it with them? Besides, in my previous life, after I died, they had clapped and celebrated, saying I deserved it. After all, once Iwas dead, my money would be divided among them. Who would pass up something like that? Not this time. This time, I would protect my money and live properly.

When I returned home from the trip, the apartment was packed with my relatives from Graves Hollow. They stared at me with resentment. My silence these past days had clearly driven them mad. Before Dad could say anything, my eldest aunt, Agnes Nightfall, pointed at me and started shouting, "You little brat, Zara! You win the lottery and run off? If Kellan hadn't told us, we wouldn't even know! "We're all family. What's wrong with sharing the money? $30 million! Aren't you afraid itll crush you carrying it alone? "There are so many of us.

Give each person a few hundred thousand, and you'd still have plenty left! We're all family. You wouldn't refuse, would you?" Listening to her made me sick. A few hundred thousand each? She was awfully comfortable deciding how to spend my money. After she finished, my younger aunt, Lydia Collier, chimed in, "Exactly. Zara, you know Kellan is about to get married. He needs to buy a house. With your money, he could finally afford aplace." "That's right. People in this family aren't stingy." "You're young. You can't spend that much money anyway.

Better to share it so everyone's lives improve." They all talked at once, but their goal was the same-to force me to hand over the money. Clearly, they had planned this before I returned. 'There were over twenty of them. Give each person a few hundred thousand, and nothing would be left for me. What a clever scheme. My heart grew colder and colder. Then Dad spoke. He shoved the crowd aside, irritation blazing across his face. "Out of the way! This is my family's money. What are you all doing here? If anyone's dividing it, it'll be the three of us- not you!

"If you want money so badly, go buy your own lottery tickets! "Where was all this enthusiasm when I asked to borrow money? You all avoided me like the plague. Now that Zara has money, you come crawling back. Don't you have any shame?" Several relatives looked embarrassed. Dad turned to me. "Come on. Let's go home. We'll talk there." I knew exactly what would happen if I went inside. It wouldn't bea conversation. It would be fists and kicks. Ipinched my arm hard until tears welled in my eyes. "I... [didn't win anything! I'm not the person in the photo. Why won't you believe me?

I just got back from a business trip. If Pd really won, why would I still be working? I'd be traveling the world already! "Everyone, that really isn't me! Please just go home!" Of course, they didn't believe me. Aunt Agnes even pulled out her phone, comparing the photo to my face inch by inch. Panic crept into my chest. Slowly, I lowered my head. a co Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.content:
Chapter 6 Seeing my reaction, Aunt Agnes became even more convinced she was right, her excitement flaring. "I knew it was you. You little liar, you still won't admit it. Well? Nothing to say now?" Tbit my lip. When I looked up again, tears had already filled my eyes. I glanced cautiously at Mom before speaking, hesitant and timid. "Th-that person really isn't me. It's Mom. Mom is the one who won the lottery." Everyone turned to look at her. Mom stared back at me in shock, disbelief written all over her face. "What nonsense are you talking about? I never bought a ticket.

How did this become me? That is clearly you!" I looked at her, pretending to struggle for words. "Mom, stop hiding it. You should just tell everyone the truth. "After all... you can't possibly spend a hundred million by yourself." The room erupted. "What? A hundred million?!" "Wasn't it $30 million? How did it become a hundred million? "Helena, you really won a hundred million?" Aunt Lydia's voice trembled. With that kind of money on the table, who could stay calm? Under so many staring eyes, panic flickered across Mom's face.

In truth, she was just socially anxious and frightened by what I'd said. However, everyone else misread her reaction as guilt, as if she'd been exposed. She opened her mouth to explain, but with so many people talking over each other, she couldn't get a word in. Finally, she snapped and turned toward me. Her hand came down hard across my face. "You little brat, what are you spouting? When did I ever wina hundred million? If I had that kind of money, would I still be here looking for you?

Tell me where your money is and hand it over so we can divide it." I covered my cheek, lowering my head, swallowing the hatred boiling inside me. My voice trembled as I spoke, "Mom, wasn't this your idea? You said we couldn' t tell anyone about the prize. "You said a hundred million was too much. If people found out, they'd all come to take it. You told me not to tell anyone, and if people called, to turn off my phone. So why are you blaming me now? "T know you don't want to give up the money... but you can't spend that much by yourself.

You should just share it." She raised her hand again to slap me, but Dad grabbed her wrist. He was breathing heavily, excitement thick in his voice. "Helena, how could you keep something like this from me? Where's the money? Hurry up and bring it out!" Mom froze, stunned. "What money? I don't even know how to buy lottery tickets. Did you forget?" I quietly twisted the knife. "Mom, you told me yourself the day you bought the ticket. Don't you remember? "When you went to claim the prize, you said you'd wear my clothes so no one would recognize you. Why are you denying it now?" That did it.

Understanding dawned across the room. Mom and I were built almost the same. We shared similar height and figures. If I said the person in the photo was her, it was believable. Sure enough, Aunt Agnes pulled out the photo again and compared it to Mom. After a long inspection, she slapped her thigh. "Of course, it's Helena!" "Helena, honestly! You win a prize this big and don't tell anyone? If Kellan hadn't seen the photo online, we'd still be in the dark!" "Helena, come on. Let's go divide the money!" She grabbed Mom's arm, trying to drag her away.

Others crowded around, surrounding Mom on all sides. Mom tried to explain, but with so many voices drowning her out, she was completely overwhelmed. In the end, she fell silent, and the scene descended into chaos. Finally, Dad roared loudly, and the crowd gradually quieted. Still, their eyes gleamed as they stared at Mom like predators watching prey, eager to tear her apart piece by piece. u (ai Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.content:
Chapter 7 Dad grabbed Mom by the arm and shook her violently. "That day, I saw two lottery tickets on the table. Was one of those the winning one? You won and didn't tell me in advance? "Helena, you're getting more and more bold, aren't you" Thanks to my earlier reminder, Dad finally remembered that Mom had bought lottery tickets that day. He shook her even harder. "Where's the money? Bring it out! With that money, I can pay off all my gambling debts. We can even move into a bigger house! Didn't you say you wanted to travel? I'll go with you.

We can even go abroad!" The more he spoke, the more excited he became, already dreaming about their future. Mom looked like she was about to cry. Not a single person had listened to her explanations since this started. Iwas the lottery winner, not her, but Ihad spoken so confidently that everyone naturally believed she was the one. I quietly stepped back, intending to watch the chaos unfold from the sidelines. Mom suddenly shouted at me, "Zara, you stay right there! Who taught you to frame your own mother like this? "Youre the one who won. Why push it onto me? You won't even share any money.

How can you be so heartless?" My eyes filled with tears. I pulled out my phone and opened the chat history. "Mom, how can you just lie like that? Our messages are right here. Look, you even transferred me a hundred thousand dollars. Why won't you admit it?" Iplaced the phone openly on the table. Aunt Agnes lunged for it, but Dad was faster. He grabbed it first. Scrolling through the messages, the excitement in his eyes grew brighter and brighter. I knew then that he believed me completely. Inhis mind, Mom was the one who had won, and the prize was $100 million.

After finishing, he kicked Mom to the ground. "You witch! You win and don't tell me, then try to dump it on Zara instead? You say you don't have money. Then where did this hundred thousand come from?" He shoved the phone in front of her face. Mom looked at it and went pale because it was her account, and the chat history was real. Her body trembled uncontrollably as she pulled out her own phone. Dad snatched it from her hands. However, on her phone, the chat window between us was completely blank. Mom hurried to explain, "Look! Her messages must be fake! I never even talked to her.

I don't know where she got those from!" Dad stared at the empty screen, momentarily confused. limmediately stepped in, sounding panicked. "Mom! You delete your chat history every day. Did you forget? Yours is gone, but I never deleted mine!" Realization dawned on Dad. Another slap landed across her face, swelling half of it instantly. Mom tried to explain, but Dad was already on top of her, beating her savagely. During the struggle, her phone slipped from her hand and landed in the nearby bucket of water. Seeing that, I quietly let out a breath. Perfect. Now the only evidence was gone.

Iwas very curious to see how Mom would explain herself now. u (aig Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.content:
Chapter 8 Dad was quickly pulled away. After all, everyone was still waiting for Mom to transfer money. If she got beaten too badly, what then? Some of the relatives restrained Dad to one side, while Aunt Lydia helped Mom onto the sofa. Aunt Agnes's eyes flickered. She moved to sit beside Mom. "Helena, why put yourself through this? You won the money, so just hand it over. Why take a beating for nothing? That's hardly worth it. You've got a hundred million. So how much are you planning to give us?" Aunt Agnes stared at her intently. Mom kept her head lowered, saying nothing.

The room fell into an awkward silence. Finally, Aunt Lydia stepped in to smooth things over. " Alright, alright. Let's leave it for today. Helena needs to rest. And you too, Victor. You could've talked it out. Why hit her? "We'll head back first. You two talk it through." She began ushering everyone out. They didn't want to leave, but since Mom refused to say a word, there was no money to be had right now. Reluctantly, they filed out, deciding to wear her down slowly instead. Once they were gone, the apartment fell quiet. Dad told me to go to my room while he talked to Mom.

I was more than happy to comply and slipped away immediately. Inside, I realized my entire back was soaked with sweat. Even though I had planned everything carefully, I had still been terrified that something would go wrong and ruinit all. Fortunately, everything had gone smoothly. The lottery winnings had been successfully shifted onto Mom. What came next would be her problem. The hundred-million prize wasn't a lie. After I won the $30 million, another ticket from the same location had hit $100 million. It even trended online, so 1 remembered it clearly.

While packing earlier, I had noticed the clothes I wore the day Iclaimed the prize. They were actually Mom's old clothes, the same ones she'd given me after she stopped wearing them. I usually wore them for chores because they were baggy and easy to move in. That day, I had worn that exact outfit to collect the prize. I had only meant to disguise myself completely. I never expected it would allow me to shift the blame onto her. Still, I didn't regret it. Mom didn't deserve sympathy. If it hadn't been for her in my previous life, I wouldn't have ended up the way I did.

Since I had a second chance, I wasn't going to spare her. Because Mom couldn't produce any money, Dad beat her again. Eventually, he dragged her toward the door to take her home. Thurried after them. Who would miss a show like this? With a sweet smile, I transferred $100,000 to Dad, acting like a dutiful daughter. "Dad, this money is all yours. Don't be angry. Mom just hasn't made up her mind yet. She didn't even need to share it in the first place if Kellan hadn't recognized her. "You should talk to her. Have her release at least some money.

Otherwise, the relatives back in Graves Hollow won't leave easily." Dad had just received $100,000, so his mood improved immediately. He glanced at Mom with irritation. "This is all your fault for hiding it. Otherwise, all that money would've been ours! Honestly, whatever. It's $100 million. It's fine to give them a little. We'll still keep the bulk of it anyway. Inodded obediently, but inside I was sneering. He didn't care about that little bit of money? He was unbelievably generous-on someone else's behalf.

If he truly didn't care, he wouldn't have been so thrilled to receive the $100,000 just now. Still, $100,000 to buy some peace and quiet was well worth it. a co Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.content:
Chapter 9 After Dad got the money, he went out gambling again. Mom walked over to me without saying a word. "Zara! You've really outdone yourself! Where did you get that $100,000? The person in the photo was you, wasn't it? It was you. It had to be you!" Her voice rose with every word. I knew I could fool everyone else but not her. Well, what did that matter? Right now, everyone believed that she was the winner. Even if she denied it, hardly anyone would believe her. Ilooked at her without expression. "Mom, what are you talking about? That money was from you. Don't we have the chat history?

"Mom, are you confused? You should go rest." She stepped forward to hit me, then, for some reason, she stopped herself and lowered her hand. I didn't bother arguing further and went to my room to rest. Half a month later, Aunt Lydia came again. She clung to Mom, crying nonstop. "Please, you have to help me! Kellan's girlfriend is threatening to break up because he doesn't have a house to marry into! "You have so much money. Just give me a few hundred thousand. You don't want Kellan to lose his chance to get married, do you?" Mom lowered her head, silent, as if numb. Aunt Lydia grew frantic.

"You can't just stand by and do nothing! Kellan's entire future depends on you! Please, just give us the money!" Mom finally looked up, her gaze icy. "I'll say it one more time. I don't have any money. I'm not the one who won. Leave." Aunt Lydia's face flushed red. "How can you be like this? You have so much money. What's a few hundred thousand? You can't be this stingy. I'm your own sister!" Mom didn't change her stance. In the end, Aunt Lydia cursed at her and slammed the door on the way out. Later, Aunt Agnes came as well. She demanded money from Mom and was refused.

Furious, she ranted in the family group chat, calling Mom heartless, ungrateful, a cold-blooded ingrate who refused to help her own family after getting rich. Other relatives joined in, piling on the accusations. Mom showed little reaction. Then again, she wouldn't know. Her phone had been ruined by water that day, and Dad hadn't been home much lately, so no one had bought her a new one. Naturally, she had no idea that in the eyes of everyone back in Graves Hollow, she had become a selfish traitor.

When the holidays came, and it was time to go back to Graves Hollow, Mom didn't want to go, but Dad dragged her along anyway. By then, she had a new phone that Dad bought. However, he had also changed her number. All her old messages were gone. During this time, Dad's attitude toward Mom improved significantly. He no longer beat or cursed her at the slightest provocation, sometimes even speaking to her gently. Mom seemed happier because of it. The moment they arrived back in Graves Hollow and relatives surrounded her, her expression turned cold again.

They still hadn't gotten their share of the money, and they had no intention of giving up. One after another, they tried to persuade her, hoping she would finally relent, but she repeated the same words: she had no money. As the atmosphere grew tense, Aunt Agnes stepped in to smooth things over. "Alright, alright. It's New Year's. Why talk about this now? Come on, everyone, dig in!" She urged everyone to start eating, and gradually the noise returned as the celebrations resumed. u ce Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 10
chapters.content:
Chapter 10 During the meal, Uncle Marcus got drunk. Staggering over, he pointed at Mom and started shouting. "Helena, how can you be so stingy? You've got $100 million and won't even spare a few hundred thousand to help us! We're family. You can't be this heartless. "Other people help their relatives when they get rich. You hoard it all and won't give a cent. You couldn't spend that much ina lifetime!" Once he started, others joined in, shouting over one another until the room descended into chaos. Some even yelled that they should beat Mom until she handed over the money.

Mom's face turned ashen. She didn't defend herself, just kept her head down and ate. 'Then Kellan arrived. He was already drunk, swaying as he approached her. Without warning, he smashed a beer bottle over her head. Blood poured down instantly, running over her face and dripping onto her clothes. It happened so suddenly that no one reacted at first. By the time they did, Mom had already collapsed, unconscious. Kellan still wasn't satisfied. He tried to lunge at her again, but others restrained him. Mom needed several stitches.

Dad rushed over to back her up, and the situation spiraled further out of control. The men were drunk, fueled by anger and greed, completely losing restraint. When things finally quieted down, someone noticed a body on the floor, surrounded by blood. It was Kellan. He lay there filthy and motionless, his fate unclear. The sight shocked everyone sober. They rushed him to the hospital. However, it was too late. He had bled out. Aunt Lydia looked at Mom with pure hatred in her eyes. After something like that, the gathering could no longer continue. People scattered, leaving in disarray.

Mom, Dad, and I returned to the house in Graves Hollow. Heavy snow had trapped several families, so those who couldn't leave squeezed together to spend the night. Sometime after midnight, a fire suddenly broke out. In the dead of winter, with all the doors and windows closed, the seven or eight people inside had no chance. None survived. Someone called the police. After investigating, they concluded it was arson and began looking for the culprit. Then Lydia stepped forward.

"I did it." "You all deserved to die!" "My Kellan is gone - none of you get to live!" Agnes slapped her hard across the face. "What does your son's death have to do with us? He brought it on himself!" "He drank himself stupid and started the fight. If he hadn't attacked first, none of this would've happened!"" "No mind of his own, and now you blame everyone else." "No wonder his girlfriend left him." "A guy like that having a girlfriend at all was a miracle." Each word cut deeper. Lydia trembled with rage, her eyes locking onto Mom.

"Helena Nightfall!" "This is all your fault!" "Tf you had lent us money, my son's girlfriend wouldn't have left him!" "It's all because of you!" "You have so much money - why wouldn't you help?" "You heartless monster!" She tried to charge toward Mom but was dragged away by the police. After she was taken away, Agnes collapsed to the ground, wailing. Because of the supposed lottery winnings, relatives from both sides had gathered for the holiday. Families from nearly every branch had lost someone. Who could remain unmoved after sucha tragedy? Only me. Inside, I felt a grim sense of relief.

All this destruction - over money that never even existed. And Thadn't lifted a finger. If not for their greed, none of this would have happened. In my previous life, they happily took my money from Dad. When I begged for help, not one of them stepped forward. They watched me be beaten and abused without intervening. This outcome was exactly what they deserved. a co Support share

chapters.title: Chapter 11
chapters.content:
Chapter 11 By the time we left Graves Hollow, half a month had passed. Before Mom left, relatives still pestered her for money. She shut them down with a flat "I don't have any", leaving them furious. Once we got back home, Dad went straight back to gambling, while I quietly prepared to leave the country. Mom had grown far too quiet. I had a feeling she was holding something back, something dangerous. It was better to stay cautious. So I moved back into my apartment. Thad planned to resign again, but instead the company assigned me to a foreign posting.

It suited me perfectly, and I began handling the paperwork. After terminating my lease, on a bright, sunny afternoon, I boarded a plane and left. Later, Dad called. He complained that Mom refused to give him money and told me to come back and help him. Imade an excuse about being abroad on business and brushed him off. Still, to avoid suspicion, I transferred him $20,000, telling him it was from my salary and that he could use it for now. As for Mom, things would take time. After that, I became busy with work and stopped sending money altogether.

In my second month abroad, I received a call from the police. An officer told me that debt collectors had come to our home. Dad got into a conflict with them and was stabbed to death. Mom had grabbed a knife and stabbed one of the collectors in return, killing him. She was arrested on the spot and sent to prison. Karma. In my previous life, I had taken that blade meant for him. In this life, the knife that should have fallen on him finally did. What surprised me was Mom. She had always seemed so frail. Inever imagined she would kill someone with her own hands. Ireturned home once.

Dad had already been buried. Mom was still in prison, so I went to see her. She was emaciated and thinner than ever before. Her expression was numb, eerily calm-nothing like the woman she used to be. Before I left, I looked straight into her eyes and said, word by word, "'I was the person in the photo. I won the lottery. $30 million. Kellan didn't lie." Her previously lifeless gaze snapped into focus. She stared at me as if she wanted to devour me whole. "Zara Nightfall! You won't die a natural death! 'll kill you! You will go to hell!" Ismiled at her. "No. You're the one who will go to hell.

As for me, P'll live comfortably for the rest of my life." I watched her grind her teeth in fury as I slowly walked out of the detention center. Outside, the sun was shining brightly, and my future was wide open. Continue Reading
